newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GRINAKER TO LIST UNBUNDLED GRINCON ON DEC 2.
newsitem.headline: GRINAKER TO LIST UNBUNDLED GRINCON ON DEC 2.

text.p: Grinaker Holdings Ltd announced on Thursday that unbundled construction arm Grinaker Construction Ltd would be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on December 2.
Grinaker Holdings Ltd's 85.1 percent holding in Grincon and a part of its holding in Grintek, representing 10.3 percent of Grintek, are to be unbundled and distributed to its shareholders.

Grinaker managing director Jack Sanlez said that after its unbundling, Grinaker shareholders would retain their shares and would receive 102.2754 shares in Grincon and 60 Grintek shares for every 100 Grinaker shares held.
After the restructuring, Anglovaal Industries would own 43.4 percent of Grincon shares, while 14.9 percent would be owned by Grinaker Construction Employees' Share Purchase Trust.
Grinaker would hold 48 percent of Grintek and its parent Anglovaal Industries would own 5.3 percent, ensuring continued control of the electronics and information technology group.
Grinaker would be transferred from building and construction to the electronics sector on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE).

Sanlez said that the restructuring, which is subject to shareholder, JSE and Commissioner for Inland Revenue approval, would allow Grincon and Grinaker's electronic interests to trade on the JSE at prices close to the underlying values of the respective businesses.
He said the company had, from time to time, traded at a discount to the perceived value of its underlying investments.

Grincon managing director Bean Bornheimer said he was optimistic about the future of the construction industry and saw future prospects in the private sector, particularly in tourism-related and leisure industry developments.
"On the international front, Grincon is pursuing a number of prospects in Southern Africa and South East Asia and is looking to grow its business substantially in these areas," Bornheimer said.
